assessment: Mutations in subunits of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) are implicated in tumorigenesis, but it is not fully understood how cell proliferation occurs in cells that lack SDH. Hart et al. elegantly demonstrate that lack of mitochondrial complex I increases proliferation in cells lacking SDH. The authors have expertly dissected the mechanism behind the rescue and show that inhibition of complex I restores aspartate production by modulating NAD+/NADH. This study thus demonstrates that compartmentalized redox changes control distinct aspartate biosynthetic pathways that promote the proliferation of tumor cells.
